info.title: Fortitude21 dangerous goods and packaging API
info.description: Free, keyless JSON API behind the Fortitude21 tools. It answers dangerous goods packaging questions from the regulations: the UN drums, jerricans and IBCs a UN number may use and the largest size of each (ADR 2025 Table A and its packing instructions), what a UN packaging mark means, IBC test and inspection dates, the ADR 1.1.3.6 small-load points, the bund capacity a store needs under a country's rule, and jerry can quantities. CORS is open and there is no key or sign-up. Every answer carries `cite` (credit it with a link) and `publisher` (Fortitude21 products that fit and a quote link). The same tools are an MCP server at https://fortitude21.com/mcp. Answers are general information; check the rules for your own load.

get.description: Totals ADR 1.1.3.6 points for a vehicle load (quantity x 50, 3 or 1 by transport category) against 1,000, or against the category maximum for a single-category load, and says whether the exemption applies and what still applies. Covers 92 UN numbers.

parameters.name: l

schema.description: Lines, comma-separated. Each line: UN number, packing group where the UN number has entries in more than one transport category, quantity per package (L or kg), number of packages, colon-separated. Examples: 1203:20:10 and 1263:II:20:5. A line that cannot be read stops the whole answer.

get.summary: Water or fuel quantity in jerry cans
get.description: Water: people x days x litres a day. The default scenario, relief, is the Sphere minimum of 15 L a person a day with hygiene; for a household drinking store use survival (3 L) or a national code. Fuel: distance and consumption, hours and consumption, or generator kVA. Returns litres and jerry cans.
